Note: RunnerPageInstance.ControlVisible reads only the control's OWN Visible attribute and never walks its enclosing groups, so a field inside group(DynamicGroup) { Visible = ShowDynamic; } reads visible while ShowDynamic is false. Fails as 'Assert.IsFalse failed. a field inside a group whose Visible expression is currently false must be hidden'.

Same missing ancestor walk as the sibling entry above, two groups deep: InnerGroup declares no Visible, OuterGroup's Visible = ShowOuter is false, and the field still reads visible. This is the case that tells apart 'consults the immediate parent' from 'walks the whole chain'.

Not #1778 either: real BC dead-code-eliminates a control enclosed by a group whose Visible is the compile-time literal false, so the TestPage reference raises 'The field with ID = ... is not found on the page'. The runner keeps the control on the page and answers Visible() = false, so the asserterror gets no error at all ('An error was expected inside an ASSERTERROR statement').

Re-pointed from #1837: the Boolean-SetValue gap that used to fail this test's first statement (Card.ToggleDynamic.SetValue(true)) is fixed for page-variable-bound controls.
